column1: # OUTSIDE_ARIZONA_BASELINE.tsv -- jcon_tests: what ARIZONA icont/iconx does not answer, named beside the
# package, so the graded denominator is the set the ONE ICON ORACLE can actually run.  ceo CEO-445, on Lon
# 2026-09-09 09:0x CDT ("Switch to Icon completely ... Get 100% using oracle probes").  Written hq_P
# 2026-09-09, MEASURED LIVE with /home/resources/icon-master/bin/icont (Icon v9.5.25a), each program
# compiled `icont -s -o <name> <name>.icn` in a staged copy and run under the package's own .dat
# convention (the companion fed BOTH as argv[1] and as stdin), 30 s run cap, 120 s compile cap.
# FORMAT: name<TAB>CLASS<TAB>reason (the oracle's OWN message, measured, never paraphrased).
# ⭐ WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AT ALL, AND IT IS THE FINDING OF THE SITTING: this package is JCON's test suite,
# and its .std files were cut by JCON.  A census of all 83 .std against Arizona icont (hq_P 2026-09-09)
# read 59 AGREE, 17 DIFFER, 4 the oracle REFUSES, 2 the oracle does not TERMINATE, 1 orphan.  `kwds.std`
# carried `&version: Jcon Version 2.2` and `&features: Java` -- so for that program the vendored oracle
# asked us to make SCRIP claim to BE Jcon.  Sixteen of the seventeen were re-cut from icont in the same
# commit as this file; the rows below are what could not be.
# ⛔ THE STREAM GAP, NAMED HERE BECAUSE IT DECIDES FOUR ROWS AND IS NOT A DEFECT OF ANY PROGRAM:
# cxtrace, loadfunc, traceback and tracing write their ENTIRE output to STDERR (icont's runtime error and
# trace reports go there), and their .std files are stderr captures -- but test_icon_jcon_suite.sh:133
# diffs STDOUT only.  Their refs are re-cut from icont's stderr, which is the honest ref; they cannot pass
# until the runner grades the stream the ref was cut from.  That is an instrument row, not one of these
# four programs' rows, so they are NOT listed below as outside -- they are graded, red, and the reason is
# written down.  A ref cut from the wrong stream would have hidden this behind a plausible mismatch.
# ⛔ tpp WAS IN THIS FILE AND HAS BEEN REMOVED, WHICH IS THE RECONCILE CEO-452 ASKED FOR (hq_P 2026-09-09).
# It is already ruled in this package's UNGRADABLE.tsv as ORACLE_CONTRACT_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, and ONE PROGRAM
# CARRIES ONE RULING: while it sat in both files the two disagreed about WHY (icont refuses to compile it
# vs we have no preprocessor-only mode), and whichever a reader met first would decide whether anybody owes
# work on it. Both statements are true, which is exactly the case lib_inventory.sh's arizona-tpp lesson
# rules on: the sufficient half is stated on its own, and the row lives in one file. ⭐ If hq_T's own re-cut
# adds geddump, htprep, prepro or tpp here, the first three are ALREADY BELOW, measured, and tpp belongs in
# UNGRADABLE.tsv instead -- reconcile against this file rather than appending to it.
# ⛔ CLASS NAMES ARE THE CLOSED VOCABULARY OF lib_inventory.sh, NOT PROSE (corrected 2026-09-09 after ceo
# CEO-470): ORACLE_DOES_NOT_TERMINATE and ENVIRONMENT_DEPENDENT read well and are not classes anybody can
# grep, so they became TIMEOUT and ENVIRONMENT_IDENTITY_IN_OUTPUT.  ⭐ The ceo's ruling is explicit that
# lgint and toby are TIMEOUT-class and NOT oracle-refused -- icont compiles both; it is our 30s cap the run
# does not fit inside, which is a statement about the cap and not about the program.
# ⛔ linking's row is GONE and is a comment instead: linking.std is an orphan .std with no linking.icn, so
# it is not in the shipped population at all and a row for it could only ever be a name the census cannot
# reconcile.  Naming a non-program in a list of programs is how a denominator stops summing.
# ⭐ MIRRORED INTO THE INVENTORY FILES, which is what makes the totals add up (the same convention the
# csnobol4 suite uses): geddump htprep prepro -> UNGRADABLE.tsv ORACLE_REFUSES · recent -> UNGRADABLE.tsv
# ENVIRONMENT_IDENTITY_IN_OUTPUT · lgint toby -> UNGRADED.tsv TIMEOUT (work owed: a bigger cap or a faster
# runtime brings them back).  test_icon_jcon_suite.sh reads THIS file to decide the denominator and prints
# every name on it with its reason on every run.
geddump
column3: icont refuses to compile it: "File geddump.icn; Line 139 # ";": invalid declaration". A jcon-dialect source Arizona Icon does not accept, so there is no ground truth for it under the one oracle.

column1: htprep
column3: icont refuses to compile it: "File htprep.icn; Line 257 # ";": missing then". Same class as geddump: jcon-only surface.

column1: prepro
column3: icont refuses to compile it: "File prepro.icn; Line 10 # $undef: too many arguments". JCON's preprocessor accepts a $undef form Arizona's does not; the program is a test OF that preprocessor.

column1: lgint
column3: icont compiles it; the binary is still running at the 30 s cap (rc=124) having written 4224 bytes. No ground truth can be cut without an arbitrary truncation point, which would be our number and not the oracle's.

column1: toby
column3: icont compiles it; the binary is still running at the 30 s cap (rc=124) having written 505,208,301 bytes -- half a gigabyte of stdout in 30 s. Same reason as lgint, and re-cutting it would also put a half-gigabyte ref in the corpus.

column1: recent
column3: Runs clean under icont and differs from the vendored .std by exactly two lines, both environment: the .std records `getenv(JCONT) = ../bin/jcont` (JCON's own build tree, unset anywhere else) and `found file: Makefile` (a listing of whatever directory the program is run from). Not re-cut: an icont-cut ref would pin THIS cutter's directory contents instead of the program's answer, which is the same defect one level over.
